verdict.question: Does the source define D with the d_lsc integral INSIDE min(1,.) or OUTSIDE it, and does (4.18) agree with (4.22)?

eq_4_18.locus: PDF page 23, printed page 22, equation (4.18), inside Model 4.7
eq_4_18.contains_min_1_note: the standalone token 'min' occurs exactly twice in the whole 37-page document: PDF p.23 line 103 ((4.22)) and PDF p.25 line 8 ((4.28)). (4.18) contains none.
eq_4_18.literal_structure: D := N * INT_0^inf psi_lsc(d_lsc) * [ max_{i,j : N_{i,j}=1} ( Phi_{d_lsc}(i,j) ) ] d d_lsc
eq_4_18.d_lsc_integral_position_literal: OUTSIDE the max; the max is the only nonlinearity present and it sits inside the d_lsc integral
eq_4_18.d_lsc_integral_position_relative_to_a_la: INSIDE, as a derived consequence: because d_lsc is integrated out inside D, the threshold P(D > T) is applied after the d_lsc average, so the d_lsc integral lies inside the survival probability and hence inside any min(1,.) used to approximate that probability
eq_4_18.derived_vs_literal_flag: D7's phrasing '(4.18) defines D with the d_lsc integral INSIDE min(1,.)' is a DERIVED description, not a literal reading; no min(1,.) appears in (4.18)

eq_4_22.locus: PDF page 23, printed page 22, equation (4.22), inside Approximation 4.9 (Wrong Guess), statement opening at (4.21)
eq_4_22.literal_structure: P_wrong ~= INT_{-inf}^{+inf} INT_0^{+inf} min(1, INT_{E(T-t)} lambda(x) mu(y) d(x,y)) * exp(-t^2/N - (d_lsc-mu_lsc)^2/(2 sigma_lsc^2)) / (pi sigma_lsc sqrt(2N)) d d_lsc dt
eq_4_22.evidence_for_the_nesting: the min's argument closes at the scaled right parenthesis rendered '!' (plain-mode line 109) BEFORE the Gaussian factor '. e^{...}' begins; the two integrations 'd d_lsc dt' are outermost. Corroborated independently by pypdf layout mode (page 23 layout lines 39-42), which preserves horizontal position.
eq_4_22.d_lsc_dependence_of_the_min_argument: only through the region E(T-t) of (4.23), which is defined pointwise in d_lsc via Phi_{d_lsc}

disagreement.statement: (4.18) and (4.22) DISAGREE as written, about WHEN d_lsc is averaged.
disagreement.on_4_18: d_lsc is integrated out inside the definition of D, so D = N * E_{d_lsc}[ max_{i,j:N_ij=1} Phi_{d_lsc}(i,j) ] carries no residual d_lsc dependence and is random only through the N_{i,j}.
disagreement.on_4_22_and_its_justification: (4.27) writes 'the survival function of D, knowing that the achieved decoding distance is d_lsc', i.e. P(D > T | d_lsc), and the closing display on PDF p.25 writes P(D > T) = INT_0^inf psi_lsc(d_lsc) P(D > T | d_lsc) d d_lsc. Both presuppose D conditioned on a single drawn d_lsc, i.e. D | d_lsc = N * max_{i,j:N_ij=1} Phi_{d_lsc}(i,j), with the max OUTSIDE the d_lsc integral - the reverse of (4.18).
disagreement.why_they_cannot_both_hold: conditioning on d_lsc a quantity in which d_lsc has already been integrated out is ill-typed, and averaging before versus after a threshold is not the same operation (x -> 1{x > T} is not affine). The two coincide only if max and INT psi_lsc d d_lsc commute, which is nowhere argued in the document and is false in general.
disagreement.is_this_a_defect_of_the_source: the two loci are inconsistent with each other. This record states that and no more; it does not determine which order the authors intended, which order their own code implements, or what either implies for the BATCH-009 implementation.

explicitly_not_decided: which of the two orders the authors intended
which order the authors' published numerical code implements
whether BATCH-009's min(1, Kbar * L^p) matches either order
any consequence for the BATCH-009 over-prediction, for Approximation 4.9's status, or for whether BATCH-010's Check B was well-directed

verdict.dull_answer_check: The dull outcome - that (4.18) and (4.22) agree and the collapse is purely an implementation choice - was available and is NOT what the source shows. The non-dull element is also narrower than D7 stated: (4.18) contains no min(1,.) at all, so the inconsistency is about the order of the d_lsc average relative to the threshold, not about a min(1,.) written two different ways.

E(T-t) := {(x,y) in R^2_+ : N * Phi_{d_lsc}(x,y) >= T - t}
lambda(x) and mu(y), the two density factors integrated over E(T-t)
Justification of Approximation 4.9: P(N_ij>0)~=P(N_ij=1); P(D>T|d_lsc) ~= P(exists (i,j) in E(T): N_ij>0) ~= min(1, E[sum N_ij]); E(T) definition
P(D > T) = INT_0^inf psi_lsc(d_lsc) * P(D > T | d_lsc) d d_lsc

alpha.locus: PDF page 9, printed page 8, Definition 2.3 (Centered Binomial Distribution)
alpha.definition_as_read: alpha in [[0, (q-1)/2]] is the parameter of the centered binomial distribution B_alpha ~ SUM_{i=1}^{alpha} (X_i - Y_i) with X_i, Y_i i.i.d. uniform on {0,1}; B_alpha has mean 0 and standard deviation sigma := sqrt(alpha/2)

source_side_links_to_the_alpha_in_4_19_a.content: a sample (A,b) produced by an LWE(q, n, m, B_alpha, B_alpha) oracle

the quantities ||P(e,s_lat)|| and ||s_fft|| normalised by the radical of alpha/2 approximately follow chi-distributions with beta_sieve and n_fft degrees of freedom; the same page then derives the exp(-alpha(pi mu_lsc/q)^2/(1+2 alpha (pi sigma_lsc/q)^2))/sqrt(1+2 alpha (pi sigma_lsc/q)^2) factor of (4.19)

'the coordinates of (e, s_lat, s_fft) are i.i.d. random variables following a centered binomial distribution with parameter alpha', giving ||(P(e,s_lat), s_fft)|| ~= sqrt(alpha (beta_sieve + n_fft)/2)
